passages.quote:
This factsheet tells you how to carry out a self-review to make sure you’re paying your workers the correct rate of National Minimum Wage (NMW) or National Living Wage (NLW). Where we mention NMW in this factsheet, we also mean the NLW.

As part of our check, we’ve asked you to review your records. This factsheet explains what you need to do.

NMW is the minimum amount employers must legally pay their workers. You’re responsible for making sure you pay your workers at least the correct rate of NMW and you must keep records to show you’ve done this.

How to carry out the self-review

Our case officer should have agreed the scope of the review with you. They should have told you which workers and pay reference periods to include in your review. The size and scope of your review will depend on factors including:

the size of your workforce

the type of work your workers carry out

the number of workers who may not have been paid at least the correct rate of NMW

changes to the NMW rates

changes in the contracted hours or pay rates of your workers

If you find you have not paid the correct amount of NMW to some workers during the period we asked you to check, you will need to check other pay reference periods. You should do this until you no longer find any underpayments.

How to work out any arrears you owe

You must treat each pay reference period separately when working out if you’ve paid the NMW. If you pay more than the NMW in one pay period, you cannot use that overpayment to offset an underpayment in another pay period.

When working out arrears, use the current NMW rates. This means the arrears due may be more than the original underpayment. To check current and past NMW rates, go to GOV.UK and search ‘National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage rates’.

Follow the steps below to work out what you owe.

Work out the original underpayment for the pay reference period.

Divide that amount by the NMW rate that applied at the time of the underpayment.

Multiply that figure by the current NMW rate.

For more information about working out arrears, including any increases, go to:

GOV.UK and search ‘National Minimum Wage and Living Wage calculator for employers’

GOV.UK and search ‘calculating the minimum wage’

What happens next

When you’ve completed your self-review, you must send us your calculations and supporting information. For each underpaid worker and each pay reference period, you need to send us:

their name, address, date of birth, payroll number and National Insurance number

details of the hours worked

details of gross pay they received, including a breakdown of any additional pay

details of any deductions or amounts they paid you

the amount of underpayment for each worker

the amount of arrears you owe to each worker – use the method above

any arrears you owed to the worker that you’ve now paid

any arrears you have still not paid

The NMW rate may increase between the date you work out the arrears and the date you repay it. If this happens, you’ll owe the worker an extra amount based on the new rates.

When we’ve looked at your self-review, we’ll tell you what you need to do next. For more information read the letter enclosed with this factsheet.

Information you must keep

You must keep (all of the following):

details of the method, size and scope of your review

details of how you worked out any underpayments and arrears

all supporting information and calculations

We may carry out another NMW check on your records in the future. If we do, you’ll need to give us this information.

Authorising a representative

If you have a representative, you can ask us to deal with them during the check. If you want to authorise a:

professional adviser to act on your behalf, you’ll need to send us form 64-8 ‘Authorising your agent’ – to get this form, go to GOV.UK and search ‘Authorise a tax agent to deal with your tax affairs’

friend or relative, please write to us and tell us who you want to authorise and what you want them to deal with on your behalf

You can also get a 64-8 by calling:

the officer who wrote to you

our order line on 0300 200 3610

More information

For more information about the NMW, you can:

go to GOV.UK and search ‘The National Minimum Wage and Living Wage’

go to GOV.UK and search ‘HMRC email updates, videos and webinars for employing people’

call us on the number shown in the enclosed letter

The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade produce detailed guidance about the NMW. To find out more, go to GOV.UK and search ‘calculating the minimum wage’.

The Acas Helpline provides free, confidential advice in over 100 languages. You can call Acas on 0300 123 1100.

If you need help

If you have any health or personal circumstances that may make it difficult for you to carry out the self‑review, please tell the officer who contacted you. We’ll help you in whatever way we can. For more details, go to GOV.UK and search ‘get help from HMRC’.

You can also ask someone else to deal with us on your behalf, for example, a professional adviser, friend or relative. We may, however, still need to talk or write to you directly about some things. If we need to write to you, we’ll send a copy of our letter to the person you’ve asked us to deal with. If we need to talk to you, they can be with you when we do, if you prefer.

Your rights and obligations

The HMRC Charter explains what you can expect from us and what we expect from you. For more information, go to GOV.UK and search ‘HMRC Charter’.

Our privacy notice

Our privacy notice sets out the standards that you can expect from us when we ask for information or hold information about you. To read this go to GOV.UK and search ‘HMRC Privacy Notice’.
